piece_type: HCP speaker program slide deck with speaker notes (PM-US-NEX-0360)

cases.claim: “NEXTSTELLIS is an FDA-approved, combined oral contraceptive (COC) containing drospirenone (DRSP) and estetrol (E4)—a novel, selective action, low-impact estrogen” | “Estetrol (E4) Has a Unique Pharmacologic Profile.” | “The Unique Dual Role of Estetrol (E4) Results in Tissue Selective Actions” | “NEXTSTELLIS is the ideal pairing of estetrol and drospirenone, delivering an effective and safe combined oral contraceptive with a unique pharmacologic profile”
cases.context: Slides 3, 8, 10, 40, 41. All estrogens act via ER-α and ER-β; no data show estetrol has intrinsic tissue-selective properties conferring greater safety.
cases.rationale: Misleadingly suggests Nextstellis is unique and a safer form of estrogen-containing contraception than other CHCs.
cases.check: Pairwise judge: do mechanism/'unique profile' claims imply a clinical safety advantage over class without head-to-head clinical data?

cases.claim: Estetrol: “Minimal hepatic metabolism[.]” vs ethinyl estradiol “slow, extensive (CYP450 pathway)” | Estetrol: “Minimal drug interaction.” vs ethinyl estradiol “extensive” (“Impact on CYP450”)
cases.context: Slide 8 comparison chart. Contribution of UGT2B7 to estetrol metabolism unknown; drospirenone component has CYP450 interaction potential; cited references did not compare estetrol vs ethinyl estradiol.
cases.rationale: Suggests Nextstellis is safer for the liver and has fewer drug interactions than EE-containing CHCs when not demonstrated.
cases.check: Judge: comparative PK/pharmacology tables that imply clinical safety advantages; verify cited refs actually compare the two agents.

cases.claim: “Endocrine Effects at Cycle 6 vs Baseline” ... “ap <0.05 DRSP/E4 vs LNG/EE and DRSP/EE b p <0.05 DRSP/E4 vs LNG/EE or DRSP/EE” | “Impact on Hemostatic Parameters at Cycle 6” ... “Significant differences observed at Cycle 6”
cases.context: Slides 17–18 from study MIT-Es0001-C201, which did not prespecify clinically relevant thresholds; slide 16: “No clinical inferences should be made from the results shown”.
cases.rationale: p-values imply statistically significant differences from descriptive data; adds to misleading comparative safety suggestion; disclaimer does not mitigate.
cases.check: Rule: flag p-values or 'significant' on endpoints not prespecified/descriptive per source; flag 'no clinical inferences' disclaimers next to significance claims.

cases.claim: E4 has “a low impact on breast tissue” | “[d]oes not stimulate breast tissue” | “[e]thinyl estradiol activates both the nuclear and membrane receptor[.]”
cases.context: Slides 9, 10, 40. Contraindicated in current/history of breast cancer; W&P on hormonally-sensitive malignancies; references mostly preclinical.
cases.rationale: Minimizes breast-related risks and suggests Nextstellis is safer, including for breast-cancer patients.
cases.check: Judge: organ-specific 'low impact' claims that contradict a contraindication or W&P; flag preclinical refs used for clinical safety claims.

cases.claim: “Unlike other estrogens, E4 has a minimal effect on the liver.” | “Estetrol (E4) Is an Estrogen With Selective Action in Tissues . . . Minimal to no impact on [parameters associated with the liver]: Cholesterol … Triglycerides… Glucose… Clotting factors…” | “Women experienced minimal changes in cholesterol, triglycerides, glucose, and glycated hemoglobin”
cases.context: Slides 10, 11, 41. PI: liver contraindications and W&P 5.6; W&P 5.8 glucose tolerance/hypertriglyceridemia; contraindication and W&P 5.1 for thromboembolism.
cases.rationale: Minimizes liver, glucose/lipid, and thromboembolic risks; references don't support clinical conclusions.
cases.check: Rule: flag 'minimal/no impact on X' where X maps to a contraindication or W&P section in the PI.

cases.claim: “Adverse Reactions (ARs) include all Adverse Events (AEs) reported…whether drug related or not”
cases.context: Slide 27 adverse reaction table; PI Table 4 lists ARs for which a causal relationship is plausible.
cases.rationale: Dissociates ARs from the drug and suggests true AR rates are lower.
cases.check: Rule: flag 'whether drug related or not' / causality-disclaiming language attached to PI adverse reaction tables.

cases.claim: [Omission] Risk presentation (slides 34–38) omits contraindication for migraine headaches with aura, hyperkalemia W&P 5.2, migraine W&P 5.4, and bleeding irregularities/amenorrhea W&P 5.11
cases.context: Slide 34: “[t]he following ISI is based on the highlights section of the US Prescribing Information for NEXTSTELLIS” and PI hyperlink.
cases.rationale: Omits material risk facts; reference to full PI does not mitigate.
cases.check: Rule: diff ISI against all contraindications and W&P headings; highlights-only ISI is insufficient.

cases.claim: “Pooled Analysis of Two Phase 3 Trials (N= 3,409) Demonstrates consistency of cycle patterns and the withdrawal bleed” | “% of Participants with Unscheduled Bleeding/Spotting N=1,864)” | “Mean Number of Bleeding/Spotting Days per Treatment Cycle (ITT Population) (N= 1,756)”
cases.context: Slides 23–25 use a definition of unscheduled bleeding excluding early/continued bleeding (~8% Cycle 1 vs ~6% Cycle 12); PI W&P 5.11 definition gives 30.3% vs 17.4%. Bleeding/spotting were secondary endpoints without Type 1 error control.
cases.rationale: Non-label endpoint definition understates unscheduled bleeding; 'demonstrates consistency' draws conclusions from exploratory data.
cases.check: Rule: compare promo rates for a labeled AE against PI-stated rates/definitions; flag mismatched definitions and conclusory language on exploratory endpoints.
